title: Scotch Game: Classical Variation
line: Black's bishop hits the knight in the center and aims at the pawn beside White's king.

steps.text: The Scotch Game. Black brings the bishop out: it attacks your knight on d4 and aims at f2.
Take the knight on c6, before Black can pile up on your knight.

also.c1e3: Guarding the knight with the bishop is also played. This lesson trades.
also.d4b3: Stepping back is also played. This lesson trades.

steps.text: Black does not take back yet. Its queen and bishop both aim at f2: the queen threatens to take it with checkmate.
Guard f2 with your queen, so the checkmate is no longer there.

wrong.c1e3: Black trades bishops, and then the queen takes a pawn on your queen side and attacks your rook.

also.d1e2: That guards it too. This lesson puts the queen on another square.
also.d1f3: That guards it too. This lesson puts the queen on another square.

steps.hint: Your queen can reach a square next to f2 or on a line through it.
steps.after: Now Black takes back the knight.

steps.text: Bring the other knight out. It heads for a square where it can attack the bishop.

also.f1d3: That is also played. This lesson brings the knight out first.

steps.text: Jump the knight to the edge to attack the bishop, Black's best piece.
steps.after: Black keeps its two bishops. You have the healthier pawns: Black has two on the same file.

summary: The bishop and queen aim at the pawn beside the king. White trades knights, guards that pawn, and chases the bishop.
